title: Oi Sobagi Cucumber Kimchi
shortDescription: Small cucumbers are cross-slit, briefly salted, and stuffed with a crisp chive, carrot, gochugaru, garlic, fish-sauce, and sesame filling.
culturalContext: Oi sobagi is cucumber kimchi filled through cross-shaped cuts rather than sliced into a salad. It is valued for fresh crunch and is commonly eaten sooner than long-aged cabbage kimchi; fillings and fermentation choices vary by cook.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Clean 2-liter glass or food-safe plastic container with headspace

ingredients.item: Korean, Persian, or small pickling cucumbers

instructions.heading: Cut the cucumbers
instructions.action: Wash and dry cucumbers. Trim the ends, then cut each crosswise into 7.5 cm / 3-inch lengths. Make a deep cross-shaped slit from one end, stopping 1 cm / 3/8 inch before the other end so each piece stays intact.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each piece opens into four attached sections.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean board and stable knife grip because the narrow pieces can roll.

instructions.heading: Salt
instructions.action: Work salt over the outsides and gently into the slits. Rest 40 minutes, turning once.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cucumbers bend slightly without breaking but remain crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep covered and away from raw animal foods.

instructions.heading: Rinse and drain
instructions.action: Rinse quickly under cold running water to remove surface salt, then drain slit-side down for 10 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No salt crystals remain and the slits are not waterlogged.
instructions.safetyNote: Use potable water and a sanitized colander and sink area.

instructions.heading: Mix the stuffing
instructions.action: Wearing gloves, combine chives, carrot, onion, gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, sugar, and sesame seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Vegetables are evenly coated and the filling holds loosely together.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare fish and sesame allergens and avoid eye contact with gochugaru.

instructions.heading: Stuff and pack
instructions.action: Gently open each cucumber and press filling into the center and between the sections. Pack snugly in a clean container with 5 cm / 2 inches of headspace.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every cucumber is visibly filled but not split apart.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean gloves and a food-grade nonreactive container.

instructions.heading: Chill
instructions.action: Refrigerate immediately for the crispest result. Any room-temperature fermentation option must be defined by the qualified safety reviewer before publication.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cucumbers remain crisp and seasoning begins to moisten the container.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep refrigerated; discard if mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration appears.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan does not use a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Salted cucumbers bend slightly but stay crisp
Finished cucumbers look moist and brightly seasoned
foodSafetyNotes: Wash cucumbers under cool running water before cutting.
Use clean tools, gloves, and a food-grade nonreactive container.
Keep refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C; this draft does not authorize room-temperature fermentation.
Discard if mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration appears.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish and sesame; check gochugaru and fish-sauce labels for facility cross-contact.

substitutions: Persian or small pickling cucumbers may replace Korean cucumbers; avoid waxed, seedy slicing cucumbers.
Use more scallions if Asian chives are unavailable, noting the flavor change.
ingredientSourcing: Choose small, firm, unwaxed cucumbers without soft spots.
Korean markets carry Asian chives, gochugaru, and Korean fish sauce.
makeAhead: Prepare the vegetable filling up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate; salt and stuff cucumbers on the same day.
storage: Refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 5 days for best crunch; this conservative quality limit still requires food-safety approval.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve cold or cool.
leftovers: Chop properly refrigerated leftover oi sobagi into a cold rice bowl within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve one or two stuffed cucumber pieces per person
Cut longer pieces once at serving time if needed

faq.question: Why stop the slit before the end?
faq.answer: The attached base holds the cucumber together while creating space for stuffing.

faq.question: How do I keep oi sobagi crisp?
faq.answer: Use small firm cucumbers, avoid over-salting, drain well, and refrigerate promptly.
